_doc: Verified covenant terms for hospital muni obligated groups, with source citations. Hospital MTIs typically split covenants between the Master Trust Indenture itself (often only a DSCR rate covenant) and bank/swap/credit agreements (where days-cash-on-hand and debt-to-capitalization tests live). Where the source distinguishes these, we record it in _notes.
_methodology: WebSearch + WebFetch against (1) MSRB EMMA OS/continuing disclosure PDFs, (2) obligor IR pages, (3) rating-agency reports (S&P/Moody's/Fitch), and (4) trade press (Bond Buyer, Becker's, HFMA). Many EMMA PDFs returned binary/encoded content not parseable by WebFetch; we relied on Google snippets surfacing the relevant indenture/covenant language for those. Confidence labels: HIGH=direct from MTI/OS/continuing disclosure verbatim, MEDIUM=trade press or rating agency summary citing the covenant value, LOW=industry-typical default (no verified source for THIS obligor).

days_cash_on_hand_minimum.citation_text: UPMC's continuing disclosure does NOT state a specific days-cash-on-hand minimum covenant. The two covenants UPMC discloses publicly are (1) Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 1.25x and (2) Liquidity Ratio of 0.6x, both tested annually at fiscal year-end under various bank agreements (not under the 2007 MTI itself).
days_cash_on_hand_minimum._warning: No DCOH covenant identified for UPMC. UPMC's bank-agreement liquidity covenant is expressed as a Liquidity Ratio (cash to debt), NOT as days cash on hand. Reported DCOH is 78-83 days as of 2025 but this is metric reporting, not a covenant floor.

debt_service_coverage_minimum.citation_text: UPMC is subject to a Debt Service Coverage Ratio covenant, tested annually at fiscal year-end, of 1.25x in various bank agreements.

additional_covenants.name: Liquidity Ratio (bank agreements)
additional_covenants.description: Liquidity Ratio covenant of 0.6x, tested annually at fiscal year-end in various bank agreements. This is unrestricted cash & investments / long-term debt (approx).

additional_covenants.name: 2007 Master Trust Indenture
additional_covenants.description: UPMC standardized its bond covenants under the 2007 Master Trust Indenture (2007 MTI). Bonds are secured by a revenue pledge of the Obligated Group. Obligated Group members include UPMC Corp, Presbyterian Shadyside, Magee-Womens, Passavant, St. Margaret, Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, Hamot, and Bedford.

UPMC._notes: UPMC discloses two bank-agreement covenants in continuing disclosure: DSCR 1.25x and Liquidity Ratio 0.6x, both tested annually at FYE. As of 6/30/2025, UPMC held 83 days cash on hand (metric, not covenant). UPMC's MTI rate covenant (if any) under the 2007 MTI is not separately disclosed; the more restrictive bank covenants effectively control. UPMC also issued Series 2025A/B (~$700M) through PEDFA in April 2025 (Loan Agreement dated April 1, 2025). Fitch affirmed 'A' / stable on March 5, 2026.

CommonSpirit Health._notes: CommonSpirit Health (formed by 2019 CHI + Dignity merger) has the most clearly-documented covenant stack of these five obligors because both S&P (Feb 2024) and Moody's (Apr 2025, Sep 2025) reports quote the specific numbers. Lead obligor issues primarily through Colorado Health Facilities Authority. Three-tier structure: (1) MTI rate covenant: 1.10x DSCR; (2) Bank/swap covenants: 75 days DCOH + 65% debt-to-cap + Baa3/BBB- minimum rating; (3) Moody's A3 stable / S&P A- stable as of Sept 2025.

days_cash_on_hand_minimum.citation_text: The most common financial covenants are (a) a minimum required debt service coverage ratio ('DSCR'); and (b) a liquidity requirement, generally expressed as days' cash on hand. These covenants are most often found in a Master Trust Indenture ('MTI'), in supplemental master trust indentures, and/or in credit agreements with banks.

_summary_by_obligor.key_caveat: Hospital MTI covenants are typically LOOSE (1.10x DSCR is most common). The TIGHTER covenants - days cash, debt-to-cap, MADS - usually live in BANK and SWAP agreements, not the public MTI. When tracking distress, monitor the bank-agreement covenants because those trigger first.
